claims.claim: DataTrove release v0.10.1 declares Python >=3.10 and version 0.10.1 in its project metadata.
claims.notes: The tutorial pins this release explicitly. Recheck release metadata before upgrading examples to another version.

claims.claim: The DataTrove Document contract exposes text, id and metadata fields.
claims.notes: This describes the version-pinned README contract; it is not a claim that all source formats contain complete metadata.

claims.claim: DataTrove pipelines are lists of processing blocks and can be run by different executors, including local and Slurm execution.
claims.notes: Executor options and dependencies vary by installed extras and environment; the tutorial does not imply that a local machine can run cluster-scale workloads.

claims.claim: The official Common Crawl example composes WarcReader, URLFilter, Trafilatura, LanguageFilter, Gopher repetition/quality filters and JsonlWriter.
claims.notes: The chapter summarizes the official example's sequence; filtering thresholds and resource settings must be tuned for a target corpus.

claims.claim: The official MinHash example uses signature, bucket, cluster and final filtering stages, and requires the final filter stage to match the signature stage's input and task distribution.
claims.locator: stage1 through stage4 comments and executor definitions
claims.notes: MinHash provides approximate duplicate candidates; it is not a semantic-equivalence proof.

claims.claim: The v0.10.1 LocalPipelineExecutor example uses tasks, workers and a logging directory to run a pipeline.
claims.notes: The chapter's JSONL example combines documented block patterns; users must install the required I/O and processing extras and test their own input layout.

claims.claim: DataTrove v0.10.1 release metadata records publication on 2026-09-30.
claims.notes: Release date is separate from the pyproject version and Python requirement; it does not imply every current main-branch API matches this tag.
